# Official Ghostty VT WebAssembly artifact

`ghostty-vt.wasm` is the unmodified upstream release artifact from
[ghostty-org/ghostty](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty), licensed under the
MIT license reproduced in `LICENSE`. The accompanying `headers/` are upstream
C headers fetched from the exact source revision below.

Retrieved using `gh api` with `Accept: application/octet-stream`. No Zig
compilation, patched export, byte rewriting, or fork ABI is involved. Artifact
identity is asserted by `src/official-engine.test.ts`.

## Bridge details

The wrapper obtains struct sizes, offsets, and packed-cell bit positions from
the artifact's `ghostty_type_json()` manifest. The manifest reports wasm32,
little endian, and version `0.1.0-dev`; its commit field is null, so provenance
is recorded above rather than inferred from the binary.

Viewport rendering uses official render-state row/cell iterators. History,
graphemes and OSC 8 links use official grid references. Variable-size outputs
are queried for their required sizes and copied before releasing memory.
The renderer-facing cell is a JavaScript object, not a patched C struct.
`hyperlink_id` is a presence marker; URI identity is resolved by cell position.

The official module has no imports. Protocol replies are collected through
`GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_WRITE_PTY`, using a tiny standard WebAssembly typed
callback trampoline and the module's exported function table. DA, DSR, mode
and color reports remain generated by Ghostty. Slots are recycled on disposal.

The existing host cell flags represent one underline flag (all upstream
underline styles map to it), and do not represent overline/underline color.
Hollow-block cursor style maps to the existing block cursor. These are limits
of the existing renderer contract, not missing VT parsing. Images, clipboard
and desktop notification effects are not part of this bridge's existing API.

`scrollbackLimit` is passed to the native physical-line limit, which prunes at
page granularity and can retain approximately one extra page beyond the limit.
At narrow widths this can mean thousands of extra lines, as verified against
this artifact (see `headers/terminal.h`). `isRowWrapped` preserves the buffer API's meaning:
the row continues the preceding row. Mode 2027 defaults to enabled, preserving
the browser bridge's grapheme behavior; applications can still change it.

Configuration preserves the historical `0 = use default` color sentinel,
including palette entries, because the public Terminal theme converter emits
zeros for unspecified colors. Omitted/sparse palette entries also retain native
defaults. OSC payloads retain upstream parser limits (OSC 8 links exceeding
the parser's 2048-byte fixed capture buffer are ignored upstream); the host
does not truncate URI results itself.
